original_card.question: Is there a genuinely unsearched, explicitly bounded improvement to the selected packing?
methods: Search a named unclaimed canonical candidate domain with a reproducible partition.
Prove a stronger scoped relaxation or exact optimum for one named residual subproblem.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Check live PR overlap first, price both suppliers and distinguish a search best from an optimum. Report the word's packing cap from ceiling.ceiling() and the fraction of it realized; label packing gains as such.

first_step.inspect: Locate the selected packing source in the review and check live PRs for the same residual problem.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Define an unclaimed canonical domain and a favorable bound before starting a new search.
original_card.bottleneck_link: An actual paid-profile gain can improve the frontier up to the other supplier cap.
allowed_variations: One bounded residual packing instance or exact relaxation.
If the coverage law, template or guard changes, derive an applicable fully charged replacement bound instead of applying the incumbent ceiling outside its scope.
scope_change_triggers: Rerunning an existing search with only a different seed as a separate mathematical contribution.

actual_scope: For the bit supplier after PR1043/PR2423: what is each further width-8 helper deletion worth (d = 0..6) under the certified optimal window-respecting re-hosting of the freed slack, for declared per-deletion local-profile models?
scope_change_reason: Drawn on the bit-supplier track (seed 14). The selected bit packing is already slot-optimal (PR1023); the open bounded question is the value of further deletions, which PR2423 left as an open question.
bottleneck_link: Bit headroom only (the complex supplier binds): it tells bit-word searches what a second and later helper deletion would be worth (about +0.08% c each under PR1043's measured delta).
stop_rule: Stop after exact optimal layouts, window feasibility, placements and certified endpoints for d = 0..6 under three declared models, with controls; no word construction.
evidence: deletion_ladder.py: unique optimal layouts for S = 45..99 (DP plus exhaustive cross-check, up to 728,466,365 layouts), all window splits feasible, audited placements, 21 certified endpoints; TEMPLATE ladder about +0.082% c per deletion (+0.494% at d = 6); controls reproduce PR589, PR1043 and PR2423 endpoints; 88 negative controls; an adversarial verifier independently recomputed all 21 rows.
author: Sagar Thakrar
ai_assistance: Prepared with substantial AI assistance: Claude Code (Anthropic, Claude Opus 5.5) orchestrated an AI builder agent and an adversarial AI verifier (independent recomputation of all rows). No independent human review is claimed.

open_questions.question: Is there a changed bit word with a second removable width-8 helper?
open_questions.why_it_matters: PR1250 shows helper 470 is the only removable helper on the fixed word; a second deletion would be worth about +0.083% c over d = 1 under the TEMPLATE delta.
open_questions.first_step: Search source-substitution moves on PR1043's R438 word for a helper whose last read can be served by a retired source.
open_questions.blocked_by: Requires a changed word and its legality/replay checks.

open_questions.question: What is the true worst-case local delta per deletion over the word's legal local moves?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It would replace the three declared models by a certified lower envelope.
open_questions.first_step: Bound the local delta of removing a width-8 helper by the minimal concave-cost change of its own climb shape.
open_questions.blocked_by: Depends on how removal re-solves other registers' frames.
